 B.A.No..14030/2025  2  2026:KER:20382  ORDER
This application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking pre- arrest bail.

2. The applicant is the accused No.2 in Crime No.1385/2025 of Ernakulam Central Police Station,
Ernakulam District.

sentences.text: The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

3. The prosecution case, in short is as follows: The accused No.1 and the applicant who are producers of film titled "Chera", induced the defacto complainant to join as a co-producer suppressing that the rights of the film has already been vested with the production company namely AP International.
On 12.3.2023, the accused No.1 executed an agreement with the defacto complainant and he invested the amount in the shooting of the film.
Thereafter, the defacto complainant claimed right over the hard disk of the first schedule of the film.

On 3.4.2025, they forcefully executed an agreement relinquishing all the rights of the defacto complainant and an amount of 1,36,00,000/- invested by the defacto complainant on different dates was not repaid and thereby committed the offences.
4. I have heard Sri.S. Rajeev, the learned counsel for the applicant and Smt. Sreeja V., the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the above crime.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicant's intentional criminal acts, and if he is released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
6. The applicant is a doctor by profession.
He is also film producer.
It is not in dispute that the defacto complainant and the applicant agreed to be co-producers of the production of the movie 'Chera'.

According to the defacto complainant, it was at the inducement of the applicant that he Dr. Rajesh Raju George vs State Of Kerala on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18733822/
2 agreed to invest in the production of the movie and became a co- producer.

sentences.text: It is his further case that he has invested a total sum of 1,36,00,000/- for the production of movie on various occasions.
However, it was noticed later on that the applicant had already assigned the rights of the movie with the company namely AP 2026:KER:20382 International.
A reading of Annexures IV to VI agreements executed between the applicant and defacto complainant would show that the said case projected by the defacto complainant is not true.
Annexure IV is the first agreement entered into between the defacto complainant and the applicant with regard to the production of the movie 'Chera'.
As per the said agreement, both the applicant and the defacto complainant agreed to contribute to the production equally.
Annexure V would show that thereafter, Annexure IV agreement was terminated.
It is specifically stated in clause 'B' of Annexure-IV that the defacto complainant could not meet his obligation in Annexure IV agreement.

It is also recited in clause 'C'
that the applicant had spent a total sum of 87,03,600/- towards the production of the movie.

Thereafter, Annexure VI tri- party settlement agreement had been executed between the applicant,
the defacto complainant and the accused No.1.
As per the terms of the said agreement, the accused No.1 took over the project and agreed to compensate the applicant.
The definite case of the applicant is that, the defacto complainant did not contribute any amount towards the production of the movie.
In none of the agreements produced as Annexures IV to VI there is any whisper that the defacto complainant had spent any amount towards the production of the movie.
It is also seen from Annexure II that the 2026:KER:20382 applicant has filed a complaint against the defacto complainant and FIR has been registered as Annexure III.
Considering the allegations made against the applicant, his custodial interrogation seems unnecessary.
For these reasons, I find this to be an appropriate case to grant pre-arrest bail to the applicant.

In the result, the application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall be released on bail in the event of his arrest on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the arresting officer/investigating officer, as the case may be.
(ii) The applicant shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting himself to the deemed police custody for discovery, if any, as and when demanded.

(iii) The applicant shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m.
and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
He shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit any offence of a like nature while on bail.

(v) The applicant shall not attempt to contact any of 2026:KER:20382 the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
